chunks: Al-Qasim from Ali from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him and his family) who said:

When the believer is taken to account, his wives will be waiting for him at the thresholds of the doors, just as their wives wait for their husbands in this world during their absence. He said: Then a messenger comes and gives them glad tidings, saying: 'By Allah, so-and-so has returned from the reckoning.' He said: They will say: 'By Allah?' He will say: 'By Allah, I have seen him returning from the reckoning.' He said: When he comes to them, they will say: 'Welcome and greetings! Your family whom you were with in the world are not more deserving of you than we are.'

key_terms.يُحَاسَبُ: is taken to account / is reckoned

ai.seo_question: How do the wives of a believer behave when he returns from the Day of Reckoning?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the eschatological joy of the believer, where heavenly spouses await his successful completion of the *Hisab* (reckoning), a concept central to Shia eschatology. The messenger’s confirmation of his return with good deeds underscores the transition from the temporary trials of worldly life to the eternal reward, reinforcing the continuity of marital bonds in the afterlife as affirmed by Shia scholars.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 3.Al-Qāsim narrated from ʿAlī, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) who said,

“When the believer is taken to account [for his deeds], his [heavenly] wives will be waiting for him on the thresholds of the doors just as wives wait for their husbands in this world when they are absent.Then a messenger will come and give them glad tidings saying, ‘So-andso has, by Allah, passed the accounting.’ They will say, ‘[Really,] by Allah?’ He will say, ‘By Allah he has; I saw him returning from the reckoning.’ When he comes to them, they will say, ‘Welcome, welcome! Your family whom you used to be with in the world are not more deserving of you than us!’”
